clinician.trajectory_summary: A 22-month-old boy presented with a 3-week history of fever, cough, night sweats, dyspnoea, and chest indrawing. Initial complete blood count showed a total leukocyte count of 98,000 cells/µl, prompting a leukemia evaluation. A chest radiograph revealed heterogeneous opacification in the right lung. Flow cytometry of bone marrow aspirate ruled out leukemia, indicating a predominance of mature neutrophils. Blood cultures were negative for bacteria. Despite attempts to obtain detailed chest CT findings and respiratory microbiological results, these were not disclosed in the provided reports.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with severe respiratory symptoms including fever, cough, night sweats, dyspnoea, and chest indrawing for 3 weeks.
Initial complete blood count showed a total leukocyte count of 98,000 cells/µl.
Chest radiograph showed heterogeneous opacification in the upper part of the right lower lobe, middle lobe and lateral aspect of the right upper lobe.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Flow cytometry of bone marrow aspirate was negative for leukemia markers (CD34, CD10, CD19, CD117, HLA-DR) and showed predominance of mature neutrophils (positive for CD13).
Blood cultures were negative for bacteria.

remaining_uncertainties: Specific imaging findings from chest CT scan (e.g., presence of cavitation, necrosis, or abscess formation) that would directly confirm the 'necrotizing' aspect of the pneumonia.
